analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־

draft.change: Link the existing Abram article to אבה through its father element and add Genesis 12:4 as an example.
draft.definition: Abram, son of Terah, later named Abraham. The name means “exalted father.”
draft.evidence: Genesis 12:4 repeats the name אַבְרָם when giving Abram’s age at departure. The name’s אָב element belongs to Haqor’s אבה article.

analysis.evidence: וַיֹּאמֶר לְאַבְרָם means “he said to Abram.” The masculine singular address תֵּדַע (“you will know”) and זַרְעֲךָ (“your offspring”) confirm that Abram is the addressee.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed preposition לְ marks the addressee. אַבְרָם is a masculine personal name.
analysis.sense: Abram, the son of Terah later named Abraham

analysis.evidence: The phrase יָדֹעַ תֵּדַע means “know for certain.” The כִּי clause gives the content of what Abram is to know: his descendants will live as foreigners in a land that is not theirs.
analysis.morphology: Qal infinitive absolute. It precedes תֵּדַע, the finite verb of the same root, to emphasize certainty.
analysis.sense: to know that something is the case
